title: Armstrong's mouthpiece, copied by Charlie Allen
summary: Randolph used Armstrong's spare mouthpiece, had Charlie Allen copy it when Armstrong asked for it back, and shows its round cushion.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Yeah, he wouldn't do it then. But did he ever talk about mouthpieces on his trumpet? What was the fellow here in town that made some mouthpieces?
Allen, Charlie Allen.
Charlie Allen.
Charlie Allen.
Did Charlie make his mouthpieces?

Yes, and I don't know whether Charlie made his mouthpieces, but Charlie made my mouthpiece like Louis'. I used Louis' mouthpiece. Louis had two mouthpieces, so he let me use his mouthpiece, so we would both blend band.
Ah.
Well, when the band broke up, I still had Louis' mouthpiece. When Louis wrote me for his mouthpiece,
then I went down to Charlie's, and Charlie --
Charlie copied it.
Yeah, he copied it, and so I have that mouthpiece now.
How did Louis' mouthpiece differ from, say, the one you were using? Was it a deeper cut?
Well, it's more comfortable. The cushion of the -- where you place your lip, is round. It's a unique thing. I'd just like for you to see that mouthpiece.
Yes, I would.
It is, it's a unique mouthpiece.
Can I help you out? I think I see the case there. Yep.
This is it, isn't it?
Yes.
Yes. And he really did do a good job on it.
Charlie passed a couple of years ago, didn't he?
Yes, he really did. See there?
Yes, uh-huh.
You see, there's nothing there to cut your lip or anything. It's just round, just real round.
How long have you had this mouthpiece?
Oh, let me see. I left Louis in 1935.
I've had that mouthpiece ever since round about -- and I gave him his mouthpiece -- round about '37 or '37, something.
When you send his back to him.
Yeah.
Is it a smaller bore than normal mouthpieces, would you say?
I don't think so.
Is it easier to play high notes with that mouthpiece than with other mouthpieces?
No, you've got to really go from your -- you've got to really have it here, to play high notes with it. See, some of those mouthpieces that Charlie Allen made, they're strictly high note mouthpieces.
Peashooters.
Yeah. And -- yes, and you -- there's something else, but I never did try to play it because I couldn't use it successfully. And I just always kept that mouthpiece.
